questions.question_text: Starting material for the synthesis of L-Thyroxine is
questions.explanation: L-Thyroxine is biologically synthesized from the amino acid L-tyrosine via iodination and coupling.

questions.question_text: One of the following antianxiety agent is an azaspirodecanedione derivative.
questions.explanation: Buspirone belongs to the azapirone class and contains an azaspirodecanedione ring structure.

questions.question_text: Include the following drug under proper classification. NIFEDIPINE
questions.explanation: Nifedipine is a 1,4-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker containing a pyridine core.

questions.question_text: Acetazolamide can be synthesized from on of the following intermediates.
questions.explanation: Acetazolamide is synthesized using 2-amino-5-mercapto-1,3,4-thiadiazole as a core intermediate.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct trichomes of Digitalis purpurea

options.A: Numerous covering trichomes and a few glandular trichomes
options.C: Few glandular trichomes and few covering trichomes

questions.explanation: Digitalis purpurea leaves characteristically possess numerous blunt-pointed covering trichomes and very few glandular ones.

questions.question_text: PANAXADIOL is a constituent of
questions.explanation: Panaxadiol is a characteristic sapogenin found in Ginseng (Panax species).

questions.question_text: The plant hormone which shows specific effect on the cell division is
questions.explanation: Cytokinins are a class of plant hormones that promote cell division (cytokinesis) in plant roots and shoots.

questions.question_text: One of the following condition is maintained in programmed temperature gas chromatography

options.A: Temperature of the whole column is raised during analysis
options.B: Temperature at the sample injection system is raised
options.C: Temperature at the detector is gradually raised
options.D: Temperature at the recorder alone is raised

questions.explanation: In temperature-programmed gas chromatography, the column temperature is increased in a controlled manner during the run.

questions.question_text: A BOLOMETER consist of

options.B: A thin blackened platinum strip in an evacuated vessel

questions.explanation: A bolometer is a thermal radiation detector typically consisting of a thin blackened metal strip whose resistance changes with temperature.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct excipient for enhancing solubility in tablet manufacture.
questions.explanation: Polyethylene glycols (PEGs) are frequently used as solubilizing and wetting agents to enhance drug dissolution and solubility.

questions.question_text: Two or more ions present together can be determined successfully by polarographevents if their half wave potentials overlap or interfere by
questions.explanation: Complexing agents can shift half-wave potentials of metal ions in polarography, resolving overlapping waves.

questions.question_text: One of the following is selective SEROTONIN reuptake inhibitor
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is a well-known selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) used as an antidepressant.

questions.question_text: Plasmodial resistance of CHLOROQUINE is due to

options.C: Increase in theactivity of DNA repair mechanism

questions.explanation: Chloroquine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum is primarily caused by mutations in the PfCRT transporter that decrease drug accumulation in the food vacuole.

questions.question_text: One of the following actions of opioid analgesic is mediated via kappa receptors
questions.explanation: Kappa opioid receptors are primarily responsible for mediating spinal analgesia and sedation.

questions.question_text: One of the following drugs has activity against Herpes simplex virus type I and is used topically. Systematic administration of the same results in bone marrow depression, hepatic dysfunction and nephrotoxicity.
questions.explanation: Idoxuridine is limited to topical ocular use for herpes simplex keratitis due to severe systemic toxicity including bone marrow suppression.

questions.question_text: A woman has to be treated for upper respiratory tract infection. Six years back she was found hypersensitive to penicillin V. The cultures now reveal a strain of Streptococcus pneumonia that is sensitive to all of the following drugs. Which one would be the best choice for the patient
questions.explanation: Due to a penicillin allergy, beta-lactams like amoxicillin, cefaclor, and cyclacillin should be avoided, making erythromycin a safer macrolide alternative.

questions.question_text: The units of measurement for conductance is
questions.explanation: Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance and is measured in mhos (Siemens).

questions.question_text: The shells of soft gelatin capsules made elastic or plastic like, by addition of
questions.explanation: Plasticizers such as sorbitol and glycerin are added to gelatin to impart flexibility and elasticity to soft gelatin capsule shells.

questions.question_text: The rate of drug bioavailability is most rapid when the drug is formulated as a
questions.explanation: Solutions bypass the dissolution step entirely, leading to the fastest rate of drug absorption and bioavailability.

questions.question_text: The loading dose of a drug is usually based on

options.A: Total body clearance of the drug
options.B: Percentage of the drug bound to plasma proteins
options.C: Fraction of drug excreted unchanged in urine
options.D: Apparent volume of distribution and desired drug concentration in plasma

questions.explanation: Loading dose is calculated using the apparent volume of distribution ($V_d$) and the target peak plasma concentration.

questions.question_text: Browne's tubes are most commonly used chemical indicator for
questions.explanation: Browne's tubes contain a heat-sensitive color-changing chemical to monitor thermal sterilization processes.

questions.question_text: A specimen obtained from a patient's cerebrospinal fluid, cultured in specializedmedia for about five weeks showed the presence of bent rods and tested positive with Ziehl-Neelsen reagent. Identify the organism
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is acid-fast (positive Ziehl-Neelsen stain), slow-growing, and can cause tuberculous meningitis.

questions.question_text: Staphylococcus aureus is used for the I.P. assay of
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is commonly specified in pharmacopeial microbial assays for determining the potency of aminoglycosides like kanamycin.

questions.question_text: State pharmacy council should have the following number of elected members
questions.explanation: Under the Pharmacy Act of India, a State Pharmacy Council consists of six members elected from among themselves by registered pharmacists.

questions.question_text: Drug combination WARFARIN/VITAMIN-K results in a specific interaction. Identify.

options.D: Harmful only in the presence of oxidizing agent

questions.explanation: Vitamin K is the specific pharmacological antagonist to the anticoagulant warfarin, reversing its effects on clotting factors.

questions.question_text: In the glucuronidation reaction of OXAZEPAM-the functional group responsible is
questions.explanation: Oxazepam undergoes phase II glucuronidation primarily via its aliphatic hydroxyl (-OH) group at the C3 position.

questions.question_text: Benzhydryl bromide when treated with 2-dimethyl amino ethanol in presence of K_2CO_3 gives one of the following
questions.explanation: Reaction of benzhydryl bromide with 2-(dimethylamino)ethanol yields diphenhydramine, which is 2-diphenylmethoxy-N,N-dimethylethylamine.

questions.question_text: Demeclocycline differs from Chlortetracycline only by

options.A: Absence of methyl group on C_6
options.B: Absence of OH group on C_6
options.C: Absence of dimethylamino group on C_4
options.D: Absence of OH group on C_3

questions.explanation: Demeclocycline lacks the methyl group at the C6 position that is present in chlortetracycline.

questions.question_text: Choose the IUPAC name for Carbamazepine
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is chemically 5H-dibenz[b,f]azepine-5-carboxamide.

questions.question_text: Reserpine is derived from
questions.explanation: Reserpine is an indole alkaloid derived biosynthetically from tryptophan (or tryptamine) and a secologanin terpene moiety.

questions.question_text: An alkaloid from Atropa belladonna having the molecular formula $C_{17}H_{23}O_3N$ having \alpha-D_22^0 when warmed with ethanolic alkaline solution is converted into
questions.explanation: Warming optically active (-) hyoscyamine with alkali easily causes racemization, yielding the racemic mixture (±) hyoscyamine (atropine).

questions.question_text: Choose the appropriate description for Ergot

options.A: Loosely arranged or in small more or less agglutinated angular mass
options.B: A pseudoparenchyma formed by the interwooving closely appressed compact septate hyphae
options.C: The crystocarps have fallen out leaving corresponding oval perforations in the ramuli
options.D: Colourless septate hyphae about one quarter the width of the cotton trichome and they become twisted together

questions.explanation: Ergot (Claviceps purpurea) sclerotium is composed of a pseudoparenchymatous network of tightly packed fungal hyphae.

questions.question_text: Characteristic bands observed in the IR spectra of alcohol result from
questions.explanation: Alcohols exhibit characteristic infrared absorption bands due to O-H stretching (broad) and C-O stretching.

questions.question_text: Bulking agent used for parenteral preparation is
questions.explanation: Sorbitol, mannitol, and lactose are commonly used as bulking agents (lyoprotectants) in freeze-dried parenteral preparations.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct non-flammable propellant
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons like trichloromonofluoromethane (CFC-11) are non-flammable propellants used in aerosols.

questions.question_text: Elastomer used in rubber stopper formulation is
questions.explanation: Polybutadiene and other synthetic rubbers (elastomers) form the base polymer matrix for pharmaceutical rubber closures.

questions.question_text: Schedule D as per D & C Act is concerned with

options.A: List of drugs exempted from the provision of import of drugs
options.B: Diseases or aliments which a drug may not purport to prevent or cure

questions.explanation: Schedule D of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act lists the classes of drugs that are exempted from certain provisions regarding import.

questions.question_text: Official method for the analysis of Ciprofloxacin is by
questions.explanation: Ciprofloxacin bulk drug is officially assayed using non-aqueous titration due to its basic amine groups.

questions.question_text: The radiofrequency radiation is associated with

options.A: Light consisting of one colour only

questions.explanation: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy utilizes radiofrequency radiation to induce transitions between nuclear spin states.

questions.question_text: How many grams of drug should be used in preparing 500 ml of a 1:2500 solution
questions.explanation: A 1:2500 solution means 1 g in 2500 mL, so for 500 mL, the amount is (1/2500) * 500 = 0.2 g.

questions.question_text: The pyroelectric detector converts electromagnetic radiation into
questions.explanation: Pyroelectric detectors absorb thermal infrared radiation and convert the resulting temperature change into an electrical signal.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of Digitalis is

options.C: Activated adenyl cyclase which produces c-AMP
options.D: Decreased Release of Calcium from Sarcoplasmic reticulum

questions.explanation: Digitalis glycosides inhibit the Na+/K+-ATPase pump in myocardial cells, leading to increased intracellular calcium and enhanced contractility.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action for Dactinomycin is
questions.explanation: Dactinomycin (actinomycin D) inserts itself between adjacent guanine-cytosine base pairs on DNA, inhibiting transcription and causing DNA strand breaks/cross-linking.

questions.question_text: One of the drugs when coadministered with Terfenadine may lead to life threatening Cardiac dysrhythmia
questions.explanation: CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole inhibit the metabolism of terfenadine, leading to toxic accumulation and fatal cardiac arrhythmias (Torsades de Pointes).

questions.question_text: Adverse effects of one of the drug include amenorrhea, bone marrow depression gastrointestinal distress and haemorrhagic distress. Identify?
questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating antineoplastic agent well-known for causing bone marrow suppression, amenorrhea, GI distress, and hemorrhagic cystitis.

questions.question_text: Varicella zoster is the causative organism for
questions.explanation: Varicella-zoster virus is the causative agent of chickenpox (varicella) and shingles (herpes zoster).

questions.question_text: One of the following is confirmed by diagnosis test
questions.explanation: The sweat chloride test is the standard diagnostic test specifically used to confirm cystic fibrosis.

questions.question_text: The conversion of fructose 1,6-biphosphate to Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate is catalysed by
questions.explanation: Aldolase catalyzes the cleavage of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate during glycolysis.

questions.question_text: Morphine undergoes microsomal oxidation by
questions.explanation: Morphine undergoes hepatic microsomal N-demethylation (N-dealkylation) to form normorphine.

questions.question_text: SULFASALAZINE is a prodrug that is activated in the intestine by bacterial enzymes. The enzyme responsible is :
questions.explanation: Colonic bacterial azoreductases cleave the azo bond of sulfasalazine to release 5-aminosalicylic acid and sulfapyridine.
